newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statpipe gasline partners take tax clash to court.
newsitem.headline: Statpipe gasline partners take tax clash to court.

text.p: Partners in Norway's Statpipe gas trunkline have taken the Norwegian Ministry of Finance to court to clarify the tax status of operations at the Kaarstoe terminal north of Stavanger, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
Partners in the Statpipe gasline are Statoil as operator, Conoco, Elf Petroleum, Esso, Mobil, Norsk Hydro, Shell, Saga Petroleum and Total.
Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the issue centred on the proportion of value added from activities which should be taxed as land-based rather than under Norway's offshore tax regime.

With effect from fiscal year 1993, the Petroleum Tax Board changed the method by which revenues from Statpipe were assessed for tax. Oil companies must now pay the 78 percent offshore rate rather than the 28 percent levied for land-based operations on part of the system's value added.

"This case is important in terms of principle as well as in its practical consequences for the Statpipe partners, since the outcome will affect other land activities related to offshore gas production," Statoil's newsletter said.
